issue.title: Lean backend can generate Iterator.next with extra back-function component
issue.body:
### Summary

The Lean backend can generate an `Iterator.next` implementation whose type
contains an extra back-function component, then assign it directly to
`core.iter.traits.iterator.Iterator.next`. The generated Lean does not typecheck.

I hit this while translating `datrs/sparse-bitfield`.

### Versions Used

- Aeneas: `a2e779f00fc384c2f4d1131bbd573dc948ddf0d7`
- Charon pin from that Aeneas commit: `9dd7f23c8458b2366ce0b5ca7529c5ad4c5fb350`
- Lean toolchain used for `lake build`: `leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2`

### Detailed Instructions to Reproduce

Starting from a checkout of `datrs/sparse-bitfield` at the following revision:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/datrs/sparse-bitfield.git
cd sparse-bitfield
git checkout 049fe04~1

# Build Charon/Aeneas (tested at the Aeneas commit listed above), then make sure both
# binaries are on PATH, or replace these commands with explicit paths.
charon cargo --preset=aeneas
aeneas -backend lean -dest lean_out sparse_bitfield.llbc
```

Then create a small Lean project that depends on Aeneas at the same commit:

```lean
-- lakefile.lean
import Lake
open Lake DSL

package aeneas_repro where

require aeneas from git "https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas.git" @ "a2e779f00fc384c2f4d1131bbd573dc948ddf0d7" / "backends/lean"

@[default_target]
lean_lib TranslatedCode where
  srcDir := "src"
```

```bash
mkdir -p src/TranslatedCode
cp lean_out/SparseBitfield.lean src/TranslatedCode/SparseBitfield.lean
printf "import TranslatedCode.SparseBitfield\n" > src/TranslatedCode.lean
printf "leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2\n" > lean-toolchain
lake build
```

### Generated Lean

The generated `next` function has an extra `(iter.Iter -> iter.Iter)` component:

```lean
/-- [sparse_bitfield::iter::{impl core::iter::traits::iterator::Iterator<bool> for sparse_bitfield::iter::Iter<'a>}::next]:
    Source: 'src/iter.rs', lines 27:2-37:3
    Visibility: public -/
def iter.Iter.Insts.CoreIterTraitsIteratorIteratorBool.next
  (self : iter.Iter) :
  Result ((Option Bool) × iter.Iter × (iter.Iter → iter.Iter))
  := do
  let i ← self.cursor + 1#usize
  let i1 ← Bitfield.len self.inner
  if self.cursor >= i1
  then
    let back'a := fun self1 => { self with inner := self1.inner }
    ok (none, { self with cursor := i }, back'a)
  else
    let (b, b1) ← Bitfield.get self.inner self.cursor
    let back'a := fun self1 => { self with inner := self1.inner }
    ok (some b, { inner := b1, cursor := i }, back'a)
```

but the trait implementation assigns it to `Iterator.next`:

```lean
/-- Trait implementation: [sparse_bitfield::iter::{impl core::iter::traits::iterator::Iterator<bool> for sparse_bitfield::iter::Iter<'a>}]
    Source: 'src/iter.rs', lines 24:0-38:1 -/
@[reducible]
def iter.Iter.Insts.CoreIterTraitsIteratorIteratorBool :
  core.iter.traits.iterator.Iterator iter.Iter Bool := {
  next := iter.Iter.Insts.CoreIterTraitsIteratorIteratorBool.next
}
```

The Aeneas Lean library expects:

```lean
structure core.iter.traits.iterator.Iterator (Self : Type) (Self_Item : Type)
  where
  next : Self → Result ((Option Self_Item) × Self)
  step_by : Self → Usize → Result (core.iter.adapters.step_by.StepBy Self)
  enumerate : Self → Result (core.iter.adapters.enumerate.Enumerate Self)
  take : Self → Usize → Result (core.iter.adapters.take.Take Self)
```

### `lake build` error

```text
error: src/TranslatedCode/SparseBitfield.lean:305:10: Type mismatch
```

### Expected behavior

The generated `Iterator.next` field should have type:

```lean
iter.Iter → Result ((Option Bool) × iter.Iter)
```

or the trait impl should wrap/adapt the generated function so the back-function
component is not exposed as the `Iterator.next` field.

The Rust-side iterator implementation is valid: `Iterator::next` should return
`Option<bool>`. The generated Lean function appears to have retained a
state/back-function artifact from translating the internal update to
`self.inner`, but the generated trait record field was not adapted to the
Lean `Iterator.next` signature.

issue.title: FnOnce problem: `call_once` return type is `Result (closure state)` instead of `Result Unit`
issue.body:
We see this problem in the [SparsePostQuantumRatchet](https://github.com/Beneficial-AI-Foundation/SparsePostQuantumRatchet-verify)
by prost-generated `merge` functions for proto `oneof` fields. The problem affects three merge functions extracted by Aeneas in that repo: `proto.pq_ratchet.pq_ratchet_state.Inner.merge`, `proto.pq_ratchet.v1_msg.InnerMsg.merge`, `proto.pq_ratchet.v1_state.InnerState.merge`.

As far as I can see it is due to `call_once`. The problem shows in the following mwe:

```rust
pub struct S;

fn f(_: &mut S) -> Result<(), String> { Ok(()) }

pub fn g(out: &mut S) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut v = S;
    f(&mut v).map(|_| *out = v)
}
```

The Aeneas generated Lean code is:
```lean
def g.closure.Insts.CoreOpsFunctionFnOnceTupleTupleTuple.call_once
  (c : g.closure) (_ : Unit) :
  Result g.closure    -- PROBLEM: should be Result Unit?
  := do
  let (_, s) := c
  ok (s, s)
```
which then causes a type mismatch:
```lean
def g.closure.Insts.CoreOpsFunctionFnOnceTupleTupleTuple :
  core.ops.function.FnOnce g.closure Unit Unit := {
  call_once := g.closure.Insts.CoreOpsFunctionFnOnceTupleTupleTuple.call_once
  -- type mismatch: call_once has type g.closure → Unit → Result g.closure
  --                  expected         g.closure → Unit → Result Unit
}
```
and an error with the return type:
```lean
let (r1, c) ←
  core.result.Result.map g.closure.Insts.CoreOpsFunctionFnOnceTupleTupleTuple
    r (out, v)
let (out1, _) := c   -- ERROR: expected a product type, got Result Unit String
```

issue.title: Limitation instantiating generic types with mutable references
issue.body:
This issue tracks minimal examples regarding the limitation of instantiating generic types with mutable references. The main categories so far are:
- `Self` type of a trait (see below for `Default` and [comment](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/issues/1215#issuecomment-5015094569) for `FromResidual`)
- Generic types of a trait (see #961 for custom trait)
- Associated types of a trait (see [comment](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/issues/1215#issuecomment-5016701168) for custom trait)
- Generic types of a function (see [comment](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas/issues/1215#issuecomment-5001571398) for generic identity function)

---

Run `cargo new --lib foo && lake new foo lib && cd foo`.

Clone or link the Aeneas repository under `aeneas`. For example `ln -s ~/github/AeneasVerif/aeneas .` in my case.

Use the proper Lean toolchain: `rm lean-toolchain && ln -s aeneas/backends/lean/lean-toolchain .`

Append the following at the end of `lakefile.toml`:

```toml
[[require]]
name = "aeneas"
path = "aeneas/backends/lean"
```

Update `src/lib.rs` with:

```rust
pub fn foo() {
    bar::<&mut [u8]>();
}

fn bar<T: Default>() {}
```

Or alternatively with:

```rust
pub fn foo() {
    bar::<&mut u8>();
}

fn bar<T: Bar>() {}

trait Bar {
    fn bar(self) -> Self;
}
impl<T> Bar for &mut T {
    fn bar(self) -> Self {
        self
    }
}
```

Run `charon cargo --preset=aeneas && aeneas foo.llbc -backend lean && lake build`.

Expected output: No error.

Actual output (relevant part only):

```
error: Foo.lean:34:13: Type mismatch
  CoreDefaultDefault.default T
has type
  Result (Slice T × (Slice T → Unit))
but is expected to have type
  Result (Slice T)
```

Actual output for the alternative (revelant part only):

```
error: Foo.lean:32:9: Type mismatch
  FooBar.bar
has type
  ?m.2 → Result (?m.2 × (?m.2 → ?m.2))
but is expected to have type
  T → Result T
```

Aeneas version: 94fc4cc
Charon version: 0.1.223 (this is the one pinned by Aeneas, namely 5a501733)

This has been seen while testing Aeneas. There is no impact or urgency. I did not test against older versions to know if it's a regression.

See #1214 for context. This might be related to #961 but differs in the fact that `Self` is in return position.

comments.body:
Actually this issue seems more fundamental, namely the lack of support for generic types instantiated with mutable references.

Here's another example without traits:

```rust
fn main() {
    let mut y = 13;
    *id(&mut y) = 42;
    id(y);
}

fn id<T>(x: T) -> T {
    x
}
```

The generated code is:

```lean4
/-- [foo::id]:
    Source: 'src/main.rs', lines 7:0-9:1 -/
def id {T : Type} (x : T) : Result T := do
  ok x

/-- [foo::main]:
    Source: 'src/main.rs', lines 1:0-5:1 -/
def main : Result Unit := do
  let (_, id_back) ← id 13#i32
  let y := id_back 42#i32
  let _ ← id y
  ok ()
```

With the following type error (on the do keyword of main):

```
error: Foo/Funs.lean:25:26: expected a product type, got
  IScalar IScalarTy.I32
```

I could not find an existing issue about this. We could either recycle this one or create a new one as "Known limitation: instantiation with mutable references".

comments.body:
Fabel generated:

> Two reproducers from a formal-verification campaign over an
> arkworks-based crypto workload
> ([PolymeshAssociation/crypto @ `zk_audit_july_2026`](https://github.com/PolymeshAssociation/crypto/tree/zk_audit_july_2026)),
> as data points for prioritizing this limitation:
>
> (a) *"Self type of a trait" category*: the blanket impls
> [`impl<R: Read + ?Sized> Read for &mut R` and `impl<W: Write + ?Sized> Write for &mut W`](https://github.com/arkworks-rs/std/blob/master/src/io/mod.rs)
> of [`ark_std::io`](https://docs.rs/ark-std/0.5.0/ark_std/io/index.html)
> (`src/io/mod.rs` lines 228 and 283 in ark-std 0.5.0) are emitted as axiom
> signatures carrying an extra `× (R → R)` back-propagation component that
> the corresponding trait field does not have, so the instance does not
> type-check against the trait (cf. #961, #1152).
>
> (b) *Generic instantiated with `&mut` at call sites*:
> [`CanonicalSerialize::serialize_compressed<W: Write>(&self, writer: W)`](https://github.com/arkworks-rs/algebra/blob/v0.5.0/serialize/src/lib.rs#L115)
> (ark-serialize 0.5.0) invoked as `x.serialize_compressed(&mut writer)?` —
> e.g. [`schnorr_pok/src/discrete_log.rs` lines 140–142](https://github.com/PolymeshAssociation/crypto/blob/zk_audit_july_2026/schnorr_pok/src/discrete_log.rs#L140-L142)
> — produces call sites that destructure `let (r, writer1) ← …` against a
> trait declaration emitted *without* the `× W` component, so the generated
> model is internally ill-typed.

(The workload actually builds against
[PolymeshAssociation/arkworks-algebra @ `be949ad`](https://github.com/PolymeshAssociation/arkworks-algebra/tree/be949ad980da003b1a43abe81c6d54dbaef8b26a),
a fork of arkworks-rs/algebra v0.5 — the `Field`/`SqrtPrecomputation`/
`CanonicalSerialize` shapes cited above are unmodified upstream API, so the
canonical links are given.)

Fabel generated:

Two reproducers from a formal-verification campaign over an
arkworks-based crypto workload
(PolymeshAssociation/crypto @ zk_audit_july_2026),
as data points for prioritizing this limitation:

(a) "Self type of a trait" category: the blanket impls
impl<R: Read + ?Sized> Read for &mut R and impl<W: Write + ?Sized> Write for &mut W
of ark_std::io
(src/io/mod.rs lines 228 and 283 in ark-std 0.5.0) are emitted as axiom
signatures carrying an extra × (R → R) back-propagation component that
the corresponding trait field does not have, so the instance does not
type-check against the trait (cf. #961, #1152).

(b) Generic instantiated with &mut at call sites:
CanonicalSerialize::serialize_compressed<W: Write>(&self, writer: W)
(ark-serialize 0.5.0) invoked as x.serialize_compressed(&mut writer)? —
e.g. schnorr_pok/src/discrete_log.rs lines 140–142
— produces call sites that destructure let (r, writer1) ← … against a
trait declaration emitted without the × W component, so the generated
model is internally ill-typed.

(The workload actually builds against
PolymeshAssociation/arkworks-algebra @ be949ad,
a fork of arkworks-rs/algebra v0.5 — the Field/SqrtPrecomputation/
CanonicalSerialize shapes cited above are unmodified upstream API, so the
canonical links are given.)

issue.title: Bug: Lean backend emits namespace references captured by structure fields and local binders
issue.body:
Valid Rust with a module named `types` and a structure field also named `types` extracts to Lean that fails to elaborate. Structure fields introduce local binders, so a later type reference such as `types.T` resolves through the earlier field instead of the namespace.

```rust
pub mod types {
    pub struct T { pub value: u32 }
}
pub struct S {
    pub types: u32,
    pub value: types::T,
}
```

Function parameters can capture constructor references too.

```rust
pub mod types {
    pub enum Kind { A, B }
}

pub fn constructor(types: u32) -> (u32, types::Kind) {
    (types, types::Kind::A)
}
```

The problem is in Aeneas's Lean name generation, after Charon extraction.

**Charon command**:
```
charon rustc \
     --preset=aeneas --sysroot=default \
     --dest-file=namespace_shadow.llbc \
     -- --crate-type=lib namespace-shadow.rs \
     --out-dir out
```

**Aeneas command**:
```
aeneas -backend lean \
     out/namespace_shadow.llbc \
     -dest out \
     -namespace NamespaceShadow -no-progress-bar
```

**Versions**:
- Aeneas: 557eff83ecef5083b98a52a94ca7fae63d6c1dab
- Charon: c8f15d7d658c86a95658f71ad99cddd4be002e04

**Aeneas output**:

```text
[Info ] Imported: lean/.build/upstream-reports/namespace_shadow.llbc
[Info ] Generated: lean/.build/upstream-reports/before/NamespaceShadow.lean
[Info ] Total execution time: 0.099256 seconds
```

**Lean translation**:

```-- THIS FILE WAS AUTOMATICALLY GENERATED BY AENEAS
-- [minimal_shadow]
module
public import Aeneas
@[expose] public section
open Aeneas Aeneas.Std Result ControlFlow Error
set_option linter.dupNamespace false
set_option linter.hashCommand false
set_option linter.unusedVariables false
set_option linter.style.whitespace false
set_option linter.style.setOption false
set_option linter.style.longLine false

/- You can set the `maxHeartbeats` value with the `-max-heartbeats` CLI option -/
set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000

/- You can set the `maxRecDepth` value with the `-max-recdepth` CLI option -/
set_option maxRecDepth 2048

namespace MinimalShadow

/-- [minimal_shadow::types::T]
    Source: '/var/folders/cq/83bfd5b96l36nmw0g9cbxjq40000gn/T/itasca-upstream-i4c75a5l/minimal-shadow.rs', lines 2:4-2:35
    Visibility: public -/
structure types.T where
  value : Std.U32

/-- [minimal_shadow::S]
    Source: '/var/folders/cq/83bfd5b96l36nmw0g9cbxjq40000gn/T/itasca-upstream-i4c75a5l/minimal-shadow.rs', lines 4:0-7:1
    Visibility: public -/
structure S where
  types : Std.U32
  value : types.T

end MinimalShadow
```

**Explain the bug**:

`value: types.T` is the problem in `structure S`. It should be:

```
structure S where
  types : Std.U32
  value : _root_.MinimalShadow.types.T
```

**Priority / impact**: This can be worked around with source renaming. But would be nice not to have to.

**Where was this seen?**:

I'm porting the proofs for my wasm validator crate from Rocq to Lean on this branch: https://github.com/eqrion/itasca/tree/lean-port

**Regression?**: Unsure, this is my first project using Aeneas with Lean.

Claude generated this fix in Aeneas to qualify names. Feel free to take it if reasonable.

```
diff --git a/src/extract/ExtractBase.ml b/src/extract/ExtractBase.ml
index 30ab2204..83f03037 100644
--- a/src/extract/ExtractBase.ml
+++ b/src/extract/ExtractBase.ml
@@ -2101,12 +2101,25 @@ let name_append_index (basename : string) (i : int) : string =
   basename ^ string_of_int i
 
 let basename_to_unique (ctx : extraction_ctx) (name : string) =
+  let shadows_namespace s =
+    let prefix = s ^ "." in
+    (* A local [types] also shadows [types.Kind.A], not just the exact name
+       [types]. Search the ordered set rather than scanning it per binder. *)
+    match
+      StringSet.find_first_opt
+        (fun name -> String.compare name prefix >= 0)
+        ctx.names_maps.names_map.names_set
+    with
+    | Some name -> String.starts_with ~prefix name
+    | None -> false
+  in
   let collision s =
     (* Note that we ignore the "unsafe" names which contain in particular
        field names: we want to allow using field names for variables if
        the backend allows such collisions *)
     StringSet.mem s ctx.names_maps.names_map.names_set
     || StringSet.mem s ctx.names_maps.strict_names_map.names_set
+    || (backend () = Lean && shadows_namespace s)
   in
   basename_to_unique_aux collision name_append_index name
 
diff --git a/src/extract/ExtractTypes.ml b/src/extract/ExtractTypes.ml
index 983e0ccb..dc723479 100644
--- a/src/extract/ExtractTypes.ml
+++ b/src/extract/ExtractTypes.ml
@@ -372,7 +372,26 @@ let rec extract_ty (span : Meta.span) (ctx : extraction_ctx) (fmt : F.formatter)
               if print_paren then F.pp_print_string fmt "(";
               (* TODO: for now, only the opaque *functions* are extracted in the
                  opaque module. The opaque *types* are builtin. *)
-              F.pp_print_string fmt (ctx_get_type (Some span) type_id ctx);
+              let name = ctx_get_type (Some span) type_id ctx in
+              let name =
```

issue.title: Improve the name matchers
issue.body: The name matchers (the Rust and the OCaml one) have strong limitations. In particuler, the OCaml name matcher doesn't handle locally bound regions properly, meaning the patterns it can match are not as precise as they could be.
